Here's a good example that I encountered just last week: a friend of mine showed me some sunglasses he was looking at on Amazon on his phone. A few days later he shows me a news article on his laptop, and what do we see? An advertisement for those SAME SUNGLASSES (served by an Amazon advertiser). Sure, it makes sense that Amazon would show you an ad for something you looked at, but damn it's creepy as hell to have stuff follow you around like that. It's ridiculous that some people consider this a normal browsing experience.

I recommend uBlock Origin to everyone now, and NoScript to my more tech-savvy/patient friends who can deal with constant unblocking. For the more inclined people, I'd also recommend Self-Destructing Cookies, RequestPolicy Continued, and HTTPS Everywhere. I say "inclined" because this combination of extensions can break some websites and force you over to IE/Edge or another browser that you haven't installed extensions to.

It's important that we push for privacy now, before it moves further from our control. This isn't a matter of "what if someone's collecting our data" anymore because we now know that there are people collecting our data, and we don't know exactly who could be looking at whatever data is collected.
